title: Lopud with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Ferries, Rules & Verdict
metaDescription: Planning Lopud with a dog: Šunj beach, ferry and catamaran rules, old town, restaurants, heat, vets and EU pet passport rules for 2027.
content:
## Dog Beaches on Lopud: Is There a Plaža za Pse?

Lopud has no official, signposted *plaža za pse*. Croatia's general rule is that dogs may use beaches unless a "No dogs" sign is posted. The practical rule on Lopud is the same.

### Šunj Beach
Šunj is the island's sandy beach, on the south-west side about 1.5 km from the village. Dogs are commonly seen there during the day, but seasonal rules can change and the signs posted on-site take priority. Keep the dog on a lead near the central beach bars and sunbeds. The quieter ends of the bay suit dogs better. Natural shade is limited, so bring water and a shade sheet.

### Other beaches
The village beaches and rocky coves near the harbour are less formal. Dogs are tolerated away from the main sunbed areas. The nearest designated dog swimming spot is at Mandrač in Dubrovnik, which is on the mainland side.

## Getting to Lopud with a Dog: Ferries and Catamarans

The crossing from Gruž port in Dubrovnik takes about 50 minutes. Dogs travel at no charge on Jadrolinija. Rules:

- Dogs must be on a lead and wear a muzzle (assistance dogs are exempt).
- Pets under 8 kg may travel indoors in a carrier of up to 45 x 35 x 25 cm, one carrier per passenger.
- Larger dogs stay on the open deck on ferries.
- On catamarans, larger dogs need a paid open-deck box. The fee is not published, so email the local sales office before travelling.

Scheduled ferries are the safer choice. Private day-tour boats often refuse dogs in summer, so ask before booking.

## Lopud Old Town, Restaurants and Walking

Lopud is effectively car-free. Paths are flat, and the main promenade runs along the harbour. The village is small and easy to walk with a dog. The roads are quiet, but the stone paving gets hot at midday.

Restaurant policy is set by each venue, not by law. Terraces along the harbour usually accept a leashed dog outside. Indoor dining is generally refused. Ask when you sit down. Keep a travel bowl and water with you, because the island has no dedicated dog facilities.

### National parks
Lopud itself has no national park. The nearest is Mljet National Park, reached by ferry or catamaran from Dubrovnik. Its entry rules for dogs are set by the park authority, so confirm leash and access conditions before going.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Pet fees on the Dubrovnik coast and islands are usually €10–20 per night. Many private apartments charge nothing, and some set a weight limit or ban dogs. Hotels are stricter than apartments. Confirm the policy in writing, including any extra cleaning charge or deposit. Ground-floor units with a terrace work best for dogs, because Lopud's stepped lanes are tiring in the heat.

## Summer Heat and the Best Months

July and August bring daytime highs around 30–33°C, with hot sand and stone. Walk before 9:00 or after 18:00. Never leave a dog in a parked vehicle, and carry fresh water.

The best months are May, June, September and October. The sea is warm enough for swimming, the beaches are quieter and the ferries are less crowded. Many Lopud restaurants and shops close in winter, so check opening before an off-season trip.

## Vet Basics

Lopud has no vet. The nearest small-animal clinics are in Dubrovnik, in Lapad and Mokošica, so serious problems mean a ferry crossing back. Pack a basic kit: tick remover, rehydration salts, paw balm, and your dog's medication. Ticks, sand flies and heat stress are the main risks. Microchipping is mandatory for dogs in Croatia. Ask your home vet about tick, flea and sand fly protection before departure.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving into Croatia

For travel between EU countries, a dog needs three things:

- An ISO microchip, implanted before or on the same date as the rabies vaccine.
- A rabies vaccination at least 21 days before travel.
- An EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet.

Tapeworm treatment is required for Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway and Northern Ireland, but not for Croatia. New EU rules apply from 22 April 2026. Old EU passports remain valid for travel. UK-issued passports are no longer accepted for entry to the EU, so UK visitors need an Animal Health Certificate for each trip.

If you drive the coastal road from Split to Dubrovnik, the Pelješac Bridge avoids the Bosnia and Herzegovina transit at Neum. Using the Neum corridor would still involve a border check, so carry the passport. Cars cannot be taken to Lopud, so park in Dubrovnik and use the foot-passenger gangway at Gruž.

## Insider Tips

- Book the earliest ferry in summer. Dogs on the open deck cope far better before midday heat.
- Pack a muzzle your dog tolerates. Staff can ask to see it at boarding.
- Skip a midday Šunj visit with a dog in July or August. The sand burns paws, shade is scarce, and a morning or late-afternoon visit is a much better plan.
- Use the village promenade for a shaded walk back to the harbour.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Lopud?

Lopud is moderately to very dog-friendly for a Croatian island. It is car-free, quiet and walkable, and dogs travel free on Jadrolinija ferries. Šunj is usable by dogs, and terraces generally welcome them. The weaknesses are the lack of an official dog beach, no vet on the island, little shade and the muzzle rule on the boats. Rating: 3.5 out of 5 for a medium or small dog in shoulder season, and 2.5 out of 5 in peak summer. It suits calm, leash-trained dogs and owners who plan around the heat.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on Lopud's beaches?
faq.answer: Yes, unless a sign says otherwise. Lopud has no official dog beach, but dogs are commonly seen at Šunj, and the quieter ends of the bay work best. Keep the dog on a lead and follow the signs posted on-site.

faq.question: Can dogs take the ferry or catamaran to Lopud?
faq.answer: Yes. Jadrolinija carries dogs free of charge on ferries, with a lead and muzzle, and larger dogs stay on the open deck. On catamarans, only dogs under 8 kg in a carrier ride inside, and larger dogs need a paid deck box.

faq.question: Is there a vet on Lopud?
faq.answer: No. The nearest clinics are in Dubrovnik (Lapad and Mokošica), about 50 minutes away by ferry plus a transfer. Carry a basic first-aid kit and a tick remover.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to drive into Croatia?
faq.answer: A microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment. UK-issued passports are not accepted, so UK visitors need an Animal Health Certificate.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Lopud with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. Temperatures are milder, beaches are quieter and the sea is warm. July and August often reach 30–33°C, which is hard on dogs.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Pet fees are usually €10–20 per night, and some private apartments charge nothing. Some properties set weight limits or ban dogs, so confirm in writing before booking.

quickAnswer: Lopud is fairly dog-friendly. Leashed dogs travel free on Jadrolinija ferries (muzzle required, large dogs on the open deck), and Šunj beach is commonly used by dogs. The island has no official dog beach and no vet, so the nearest care is in Dubrovnik. Visit in May, June, September or October.
